## The capstone decision {#ch18-01 .balanced .stepwise}

Which product families should Charles River make, buy, or reprice?

What must happen to capacity and cost for that recommendation to work?

::: {.notes}
Purpose: introduce the independent management decision. Allow 60-90 seconds. The case places the CFO and production manager at an August 2027 decision meeting. They disagree about what the reported manufacturing cost means. Students must test the premises, compare relevant alternatives, and make a family-by-family recommendation whose assumptions are visible. Misconception to address: the lowest reported full cost automatically identifies the best decision. Pause and ask: Which costs would actually change if one family were bought? Transition: define the learning objectives.
:::

## Learning objectives {#ch18-02 .balanced .stepwise}

- Test cost behavior and measure practical capacity.
- Explain three product-costing views.
- Evaluate outsourcing, capacity, and pricing alternatives.
- Defend revised standards and a decision memo.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: describe the capabilities the submission should demonstrate. Allow 60-90 seconds. The assignment combines extraction, modeling, and communication. Students should explain why costing views disagree, what drives a decision boundary, and which evidence supports their assumptions. A decision maker should be able to change a key input and see the consequences without rebuilding the analysis. Misconception to address: a technically elaborate model is enough without a recommendation. Pause and ask: Which sensitivity would be most useful in the meeting? Transition: establish the common case inputs.
:::

## Use one common set of case inputs {#ch18-03 .balanced .stepwise}

Fiscal 2026 is the base year.

The supplier quote is a hypothetical case exhibit.

Keep the quote and planning assumptions on one Assumptions sheet.

[Quote](https://aa.accountinganalyticshub.com/chapters/18-make-buy-or-reprice/chapter.html#tbl-18-01) · [Planning assumptions](https://aa.accountinganalyticshub.com/chapters/18-make-buy-or-reprice/chapter.html#tbl-18-02)

::: {.notes}
Purpose: distinguish supplied assumptions from observations. Allow 60-90 seconds. The quote is not a database table or a market price retrieved for this project. Use the public exhibit and the controller's assumptions as the shared starting point. Record any sensitivity separately from that base. Preserve the quote's terms as well as the price per unit. Misconception to address: a case assumption should be presented as an empirical finding. Pause and ask: Which assumption will you test rather than silently replace? Transition: set up the deliverables.
:::

## Assign a role to each working file {#ch18-04 .balanced}

| File | Main responsibility |
|---|---|
| MakeBuy.sql | Reconciled family, activity, and capacity inputs |
| Make Buy Reprice.xlsx | Formulas, assumptions, and decisions |
| Product Costs.pbix | Costing-view explorer and validation |

::: {.notes}
Purpose: organize the tool handoffs. Allow 60-90 seconds. Use CharlesRiver_Capstone.sqlite as the working copy and preserve the original download. The workbook should keep item costs in a named Table so the report can load them. Document query populations, export dates, definitions, and the checks that reconcile each handoff. Misconception to address: copying a query result into a workbook transfers all its context automatically. Pause and ask: Which identifiers must survive the item-cost handoff? Transition: sequence the four milestones.
:::

## Four milestones lead to the recommendation {#ch18-05 .balanced .stepwise}

1. Establish what the records show.
2. Compute and reconcile the costing views.
3. Evaluate make, buy, capacity, and price.
4. Propose standards and communicate the decision.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: show the dependency between phases. Allow 60-90 seconds. The decision stage depends on the cost-behavior and capacity evidence. A revised standard also requires an explicit capacity basis. Review each milestone before using its outputs in the next, and preserve unresolved assumptions so they remain visible in the final memo. Misconception to address: the supplier comparison can be completed before classifying the costs. Pause and ask: Which error could change every family recommendation? Transition: test the recorded baseline.
:::

# Milestone 1: what the records show {#ch18-module-6}

::: {.notes}
Requirements 1 to 3 test the CFO's comparison, classify the manufacturing inputs, and measure activities and capacity. Begin with reconciliations.
:::

## Test the premises before accepting the comparison {#ch18-07 .balanced .stepwise}

Reconcile family variances to account 5080.

Keep sales, closes, and completions at their own grains.

Test the history of standards and list prices.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: separate a management claim from its evidence. Allow 60-90 seconds. The CFO's opening comparison is the question to investigate. Extract the required family results and explain the periods and allocation bases used by each margin view. Purchased products in the same family are different items, so they are a comparison population rather than interchangeable substitutes. Misconception to address: joining all the detail tables produces a valid family total automatically. Pause and ask: Which join is most likely to multiply a family's variance? Transition: reconstruct the manufacturing inputs.
:::

## Measure the inputs to clearing, not every debit {#ch18-08 .balanced .stepwise}

Identify payroll, factory overhead, and depreciation inputs.

Separate the standard cost released by completions.

Keep favorable close postings out of the input definition.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: define the manufacturing-cost population. Allow 60-90 seconds. Account 1090 contains different kinds of postings. The public requirement specifies which sources represent manufacturing inputs and which transfer or clear balances. A simple sum of all debits can therefore answer the wrong question. Retain source-document types and the reconciliation to the ledger. Misconception to address: a debit to clearing always represents a new production resource cost. Pause and ask: What posting could return a favorable variance to the account? Transition: test cost behavior over comparable months.
:::

## Cost behavior is a hypothesis to test {#ch18-09 .balanced .stepwise}

Compare monthly inputs with completed standard hours.

Explain startup and pay-calendar effects.

Support each classification with a model and business reasoning.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: connect regression evidence with cost classification. Allow 60-90 seconds. Use the months and source populations specified in the assignment. Inspect the pattern and calendar before interpreting a regression coefficient. A statistical association helps assess the hypothesis but does not by itself establish whether the cost will stop under an outsourcing decision. Extract January 2024 through December 2026. Fit the regression and test cost behavior from February 2024 onward, then explain how including January 2024 and the months with three pay dates affects the interpretation. Misconception to address: a high correlation proves that a cost is immediately avoidable. Pause and ask: Could an apparently fixed cost change only after a management action? Transition: measure the resources used.
:::

## Measure activities and practical capacity separately {#ch18-10 .balanced .stepwise}

Routing run time and setup time describe resource use.

WorkCenterCalendar describes available hours.

Apply the case's practical-capacity assumption explicitly.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: distinguish a usage estimate from the supply of capacity. Allow 60-90 seconds. Allocate setup according to the family's batch evidence and retain work-center detail. Routing time is a defined measure of required activity, not proof of every hour actually worked. Practical capacity and observed use answer different questions and should remain separate in the workbook. Misconception to address: unused capacity can be inferred from sales units alone. Pause and ask: What activity is omitted if you use run time without setup? Transition: accept the first milestone.
:::

## Milestone 1 checkpoint {#ch18-11 .balanced .stepwise}

Do the family and clearing totals reconcile?

Does each cost classification have supporting evidence?

Can you explain available, practical, and used hours?

[Open Requirements 1-3](https://aa.accountinganalyticshub.com/chapters/18-make-buy-or-reprice/chapter.html#phase-1-what-the-records-show)

::: {.notes}
Purpose: review the baseline before pricing alternatives. Allow 3-5 minutes. Ask teams to show one ledger reconciliation and one cost-behavior classification. They should name the data window, grain, and limitation of the capacity measure. An unresolved control difference should be corrected before it becomes a product-cost input. Misconception to address: a plausible unit cost is enough to accept the baseline. Pause and ask: Which assumption will receive a sensitivity analysis next? Transition: build the three cost views.
:::

# Milestone 2: what a product costs {#ch18-module-12}

::: {.notes}
Requirements 4 and 5 build three reconciled costing views and an explorer for the decision meeting.
:::

## Three costing views answer different questions {#ch18-13 .balanced}

| View | What it assigns to products |
|---|---|
| Standard | The defined standard resource rates |
| Actual absorption | The period's cost spread over output |
| Time-driven | Capacity used at its practical-capacity rate |

::: {.notes}
Purpose: explain the models before comparing their results. Allow 60-90 seconds. Each view has a different treatment of the cost left outside or inside products. Students should be able to explain that treatment without referring to a particular family's result. The assignment specifies the input definitions and allocation bases; document them alongside the formulas. Misconception to address: one costing method is universally correct for every decision. Pause and ask: Where does unused capacity appear under each view? Transition: keep unused capacity visible.
:::

## Reconcile used resources and unused capacity {#ch18-14 .balanced .stepwise}

Compute item costs from the required inputs.

Show unused capacity on its own line.

Reconcile the manufacturing resource components to account 1090.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: retain the accounting control across cost views. Allow 60-90 seconds. The model must explain where the supplied resource cost goes. Keep material components and manufacturing-clearing components distinct when performing the reconciliation. A residual should not be labeled unused capacity merely because the spreadsheet needs a balancing amount; derive it from the stated resource and usage model. Misconception to address: a reconciliation plug measures a real resource category. Pause and ask: Which independently measured inputs support the unused-capacity amount? Transition: test the capacity assumption.
:::

## Test which conclusions depend on practical capacity {#ch18-15 .balanced .stepwise}

Use the assigned range of capacity percentages.

Observe the effect on unit cost and unused capacity.

Identify recommendations that change within the range.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: turn a shared assumption into a visible sensitivity. Allow 60-90 seconds. Keep the base-case assumption intact while a Data Table varies it. Describe why changing the denominator changes a resource rate and which other components should remain stable. The point is to identify the decision's dependence on the assumption, not select the most favorable percentage. Excel requires the Data Table input cell to be on the same worksheet as the Data Table. Keep the practical-share input used by the cost formulas on that worksheet while testing the assigned 75% to 90% range. Misconception to address: sensitivity analysis proves which assumption is true. Pause and ask: Which conclusion is robust across the assigned range? Transition: build the meeting explorer.
:::

## The explorer must use the workbook's definitions {#ch18-16 .balanced .stepwise}

Load the item-cost Table and preserve its keys.

Let a slicer select the costing view.

Validate each selected view against the workbook.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: make the report a controlled consumer of the model. Allow 60-90 seconds. Use the disconnected-table pattern from Chapter 15 to select a defined cost measure. Handle items without a cost-table row deliberately, including the services population described in the case. Provide About, Validation, and Tests surfaces so the meeting display does not become a separate authority. Misconception to address: a Blank item group should be hidden without investigating its source. Pause and ask: How will you prove that a selected costing view matches the workbook? Transition: accept the cost-model milestone.
:::

## Milestone 2 checkpoint {#ch18-17 .balanced .stepwise}

Can each cost view be explained and reconciled?

Is unused capacity explicit?

Does changing the report view reproduce the workbook?

[Open Requirements 4-5](https://aa.accountinganalyticshub.com/chapters/18-make-buy-or-reprice/chapter.html#phase-2-what-a-product-costs)

::: {.notes}
Purpose: accept the model before recommending action. Allow 3-5 minutes. Ask a team member who did not build a formula to explain its inputs and cost treatment. Demonstrate one report selection and its independent control. Preserve both the base case and the sensitivity evidence for the next phase. Misconception to address: agreement between two copied values constitutes an independent test. Pause and ask: What control would detect a duplicated item-cost row? Transition: compare relevant alternatives.
:::

# Milestone 3: make, buy, or reprice {#ch18-module-18}

::: {.notes}
Requirements 6 to 8 evaluate family choices, released capacity, and price changes. State the action required for a cost to change.
:::

## Relevant cost depends on what actually stops {#ch18-19 .balanced .stepwise}

Compare the delivered quote with avoidable costs.

Evaluate the crew-kept and crew-reduced cases separately.

Keep supervision, depreciation, and other retained costs visible.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: separate a reported product cost from an incremental decision. Allow 60-90 seconds. Buying a family changes some resource demands, but it does not automatically reduce cash outlays for every allocated cost. The assignment requires two crew cases so the saving is conditional on a stated action. Decisions about positions remain with the production manager. Misconception to address: removing an allocation removes the underlying cost. Pause and ask: What must happen before released crew time becomes a monetary saving? Transition: include the full supplier terms.
:::

## The supplier comparison includes more than unit price {#ch18-20 .balanced .stepwise}

Freight, minimum volume, and the fixed-price term.

Tooling, qualification, and any severance.

Lead time, quality responsibilities, and payment terms.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: evaluate the quote as a complete alternative. Allow 60-90 seconds. The public quote exhibit supplies assumptions beyond its average price. Use the same family mix and volume basis when comparing alternatives, and distinguish recurring annual effects from one-time costs. The case asks for the combined effect over the quoted price horizon. Misconception to address: the quoted price alone is the cost of buying. Pause and ask: Which condition could make an apparently favorable unit comparison unattractive? Transition: locate the decision boundary.
:::

## Show the conditions that change the recommendation {#ch18-21 .balanced .stepwise}

Use Goal Seek for each break-even quote.

Vary quote and the share of crew time actually removed.

State the terms that the numerical model does not settle.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: make the recommendation conditional and testable. Allow 60-90 seconds. A decision table is more useful when it shows the point at which the preferred alternative changes. Keep the model's sign convention clear and distinguish the base case from sensitivity inputs. Explain the difference between the relevant-cost result and the CFO's absorption-cost comparison. Misconception to address: a sensitivity table replaces the need to select and justify a base recommendation. Pause and ask: Which condition would you monitor after the contract starts? Transition: value the capacity released.
:::

## Released hours are an option, not automatic value {#ch18-22 .balanced .stepwise}

Identify the work centers where hours are freed.

Compare released hours with existing unused capacity.

Evaluate a feasible use or removal of the resource.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: prevent a mechanical opportunity-cost claim. Allow 60-90 seconds. Freed time can matter if the business has a valuable feasible use for it or can remove the related cost. The assignment also offers an optional constrained-growth model. If using Solver, state the objective, constraints, binding work centers, and interpretation of the result under the assumed growth case. Misconception to address: every released hour earns its accounting rate as a benefit. Pause and ask: What evidence would establish a valuable alternative use? Transition: test the pricing alternative.
:::

## A price target needs a volume-risk comparison {#ch18-23 .balanced .stepwise}

Calculate the price needed for the assigned margin floor.

Measure how much volume the increase could lose.

Assess the available evidence on customer response.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: connect a cost-based target with contribution consequences. Allow 60-90 seconds. Goal Seek can find a price that meets a mathematical target, but demand response determines whether it is a sensible action. Use contribution over the relevant crew-kept cost for the assigned volume-loss calculation. Promotion history and price-list use provide evidence with limitations, not a guaranteed demand curve. Misconception to address: meeting a margin floor guarantees higher total contribution. Pause and ask: What change in customer behavior would overturn the recommendation? Transition: accept the decision milestone.
:::

## Milestone 3 checkpoint {#ch18-24 .balanced .stepwise}

Is each recommendation family-specific?

Are annual effects and one-time costs separate?

Are capacity and demand assumptions visible?

[Open Requirements 6-8](https://aa.accountinganalyticshub.com/chapters/18-make-buy-or-reprice/chapter.html#phase-3-make-buy-or-reprice)

::: {.notes}
Purpose: review decisions before revising the standards. Allow 3-5 minutes. Ask teams to defend one decision boundary and one qualitative condition. The purchased products already in a family are different items and should not be treated as exact substitutes. Make the required production-manager decision explicit without deciding staffing positions on that manager's behalf. Misconception to address: a companywide average decision is sufficient for all families. Pause and ask: Which family recommendation is most sensitive to the assumptions? Transition: consider the reporting consequences.
:::

# Milestone 4: standards and the memo {#ch18-module-25}

::: {.notes}
Requirements 9 and 10 address the proposed standard, its statement effects, and the communication to the two decision makers.
:::

## A revised standard needs a stated capacity basis {#ch18-26 .balanced .stepwise}

Build the proposed rate from the assigned normal-capacity plan.

Compare it with current standards and the other cost views.

Explain the treatment of unused and abnormal capacity costs.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: separate a planning standard from an actual-volume absorption rate. Allow 60-90 seconds. The case directs students to the inventory accounting guidance and the supplied normal-capacity plan. Document the basis before revaluing inventory. An observed high actual unit cost should not be imported into a standard without explaining what it contains and whether that treatment is appropriate. Misconception to address: the latest actual unit cost is automatically the best standard. Pause and ask: Which part of the standard reflects a capacity assumption? Transition: measure the comparative reporting effect.
:::

## Trace the proposed standard into inventory and income {#ch18-27 .balanced .stepwise}

Identify the manufactured goods still held at each year-end.

Track opening retained earnings and each period's income effect.

Evaluate the consequences for already issued statements.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: make the reporting implications part of the decision. Allow 60-90 seconds. Students must determine the affected inventory population and show how the revaluation moves across the comparative periods. Use the case's materiality condition and assigned accounting guidance to support the proposed treatment. The briefing does not select that judgment for the team. Misconception to address: a decision model can ignore the effect of changing the inventory standard. Pause and ask: Which evidence connects an item cost to units still on hand? Transition: write the decision memo.
:::

## The memo needs a decision table and clear conditions {#ch18-28 .balanced .stepwise}

Family, recommended action, annual effect, and one-time cost.

The assumptions and conditions supporting each action.

Proposed standards, statement implications, and the remaining management decision.

::: {.notes}
Purpose: focus the final communication on action. Allow 60-90 seconds. The case limits the memo to two pages with an exhibit appendix of no more than three pages. Address both the CFO and production manager's concerns. Use the table to make disagreements about assumptions visible rather than burying them in formulas. Retain the evidence behind each recommendation. Misconception to address: the memo should retell every modeling step in order. Pause and ask: Which exhibit best explains why the decision differs from an absorption-cost comparison? Transition: check the final submission.
:::

## Deliver a model the meeting can challenge {#ch18-29 .balanced .stepwise}

Documented SQL and workbook with one Assumptions sheet.

Product Costs.pbix with About, Validation, and Tests.

Decision memo and concise exhibit appendix.

[Open the submission checklist](https://aa.accountinganalyticshub.com/chapters/18-make-buy-or-reprice/chapter.html#deliverables-and-checklist)

::: {.notes}
Purpose: close with a reproducible handoff. Allow 2-3 minutes. Use the chapter checklist to verify the required sheets, cost table, report pages, tests, and memo limits. Reopen the files, change one documented sensitivity input, and confirm that the intended outputs respond. Restore the chosen base case and retain the validation evidence with the submission. Misconception to address: an impressive explorer can substitute for transparent workbook formulas. Pause and ask: Can another analyst reproduce the base recommendation from the saved files? Transition: acknowledge the assigned readings.
:::
